To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Hologic QDRA and QDRA densitometers underestimated fat mass (FM), and the QDRA underestimated FM more than the QDRA.
the Hologic QD4500A and Hologic QD2000 densitometer under-estimated fat mass (FM; QD4500: 3.3 ± 2.3 kg, P <.0001; QD2000: 0.9 ± 1.2 kg, P <.0001) when compared to deuterium diluion.
both Hologic QDR densitometers underestimate body fat in children, and that the QDR-450 0A provides a greater underestimate than the QDR 2000.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of the Hologic QD-4500A dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) densitometer in estimating body fat in children.
the use of dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) for the assessment of body composition.
the development of new techniques for measuring the amount of body fat in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both instruments underestimate FM, but the QDR-450 0A underestimates more than does the QDR-2 000.
the QDR-450A is not a valid instrument for the measurement of FM in children.
neither the QDR-450 or QDR-200 are appropriate for the assessment of body composition in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hologic QDRA-4500A is not a valid instrument for the assessment of FM in children.
the QDR-450A and QDR2000 are not suitable for measuring body composition in children.
neither of these densitometers should be used for estimation of children’s FM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QDR-450A is not an accurate measure of body fat in children.
neither of these densitometers is suitable for use in longitudinal studies of children's fatness.
neither densitometry system should be used for the estimation of FM in children, and that further work is needed to develop a valid method of measuring FM in this population.
